source.citation: Reisecker, V., Flatscher, F., Porz, L., et al. Effect of pulse-current-based protocols on the lithium dendrite formation and evolution in all-solid-state batteries. Nat. Commun. 14, 2432 (2023)
source.licence: CC BY 4.0 (article and SI files; peer-review file states CC BY 4.0 explicitly)
source.data_availability_statement: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. (No numeric source data published.)

stack_pressure_kPa.source: Supp. Note 2; main text says '<3 kPa'

global_conditions.atmosphere: Ar glovebox, O2 and H2O < 1 ppm (stated, Methods)
global_conditions.cell: symmetric Li:Sn (70:30 wt%) | LLZTO | Li:Sn, pellet clamped between two parallel brass current collectors (Supp. Fig. 21c) (stated)
global_conditions.pulsed_protocol: PP = 1:1 us pulse/pause (1 us current on, 1 us off) for all SC and HP pulsed experiments (stated, Supp. Note 3)
global_conditions.ccd_eff_definition: CCD_eff = CCD / 2 for 1:1 pulsing (plated-capacity basis); equal to CCD for DC (stated, Results)
global_conditions.current_program: stepwise increasing galvanostatic cycling until failure (stated: CCD = current density where the characteristic potential drop starts; Supp. Note 5; Supp. Figs 9-10 show the ramp)

optical_imaging_interval_s.source: Methods: 'images recorded on a 2-7 s period'

quantities.quantity: definition of dendrite growth rate in Fig. 3e,f
quantities.value: distance between the electrodes divided by the time needed for the dendrite to reach the opposing electrode
quantities.notes: An average over the whole crossing. It is not a tip velocity. The start time (initiation vs current switch) is not defined.

growth rate vs CCD_eff, every plotted point in Fig. 3e (SC) and Fig. 3f (HP)

uncertainty.note: Marker centres and axis ticks read as exact vector path coordinates from the publisher PDF; uncertainty = axis-tick linear-fit residual + 0.01 pt + rounding. The marker half-widths (SC: 0.10-0.14 mA/cm2, 0.9-1.3 um/s; HP: 0.07-0.10 mA/cm2, 0.6-0.8 um/s) bound any visual reading. No error bars are drawn in the figure.

quantities.notes: IMPORTANT: Fig. 3e is single crystal (DC and PP), Fig. 3f is hot-pressed (DC and PP). The panels are NOT 'DC vs pulsed'. Cross-check against Supp. Tables 3-4: HP DC x-values match the tabulated CCD_eff to <=0.002 mA/cm2; several SC points and HP PP 2 are offset by 0.05-0.12 mA/cm2; SC PP 1 (1.765) and HP PP 7 (2.4) are not plotted; the 3 low-quality SC DC samples are not plotted. Figure caption has a likely typo: 'green (HP DC)' should be HP PP.

quantities.quantity: endpoints and slopes of the trend lines drawn in Fig. 3e,f
quantities.notes: The caption says the trends are coloured 'for visualization purposes'. They are not the stated fits.

quantities.quantity: least-squares slopes of the digitised points
quantities.notes: SC slopes are within ~10% of the stated values. The HP slopes (13.7 and 1.1 stated) cannot be reproduced from the plotted points. Treat the stated HP slopes as unverified.

quantities.quantity: per-sample CCD, CCD_eff, ASR, current step

uncertainty.value: the current step size (50-250 uA/cm2), per sample
uncertainty.note: The paper quotes CCD as 'max value - step size'

quantities.notes: Supp. Tab. 4 is not a Word table object; it was extracted from the docx XML. The stated means reproduce from the tables: SC DC 2.7+/-2.0 (excluding the 3 low-quality samples), HP DC 0.6+/-0.3, HP PP 3.3+/-1.8 (eff 1.7+/-0.9). Exception: SC PP gives 2.38+/-1.52 (eff 1.19+/-0.76), but the text states 2.1+/-1.6 (eff 1.0+/-0.8).
The Supp. Fig. 9 caption gives the highest SC effective CCD as (4.59 +/- 0.05). This conflicts with the 4.95 in the table and main text, probably a digit transposition.

uncertainty.note: '~' in Methods, 'roughly' in Results. The two statements disagree for HP.

source.text: Methods 'Sample preparation'; Results 'Ensure minimum sample-to-sample variation'

quantities.notes: Per-sample dimensions are not given. The paper does not state which dimension is the electrode gap.

quantities.quantity: sample contact area used for the pressure estimate
quantities.notes: Derived inference: 1.84 mm2 = 2.3 x 0.8 mm, the HP width x thickness face. So the HP electrode faces are width x thickness and the HP gap would be the 2.5 mm length. The same convention would give an SC gap of 3.3 mm, but the movie frames (below) suggest the gap is the SHORTER visible dimension. Unresolved.

movie3.via: Fig. 3a 'diffuse' bar / Fig. 3b bar (same sample, the two bars disagree by 5%)

movie4.conflict: Supp. Figs 9 and 12 '0.1 cm' bars on the same sample give 237-262 px/mm

movie5.via: Supp. Fig. 11c / Supp. Fig. 10 '0.1 cm' bars (no Fig. 3a panel matches Movie 5)

uncertainty.value: at least 5%; up to 1.6x between bar sources
uncertainty.note: Similarity transform from SIFT+RANSAC, rotation -90 deg (Fig. 3a is the movie frame rotated 90 deg; movie 4 -85.9 deg). The registration scale is stable to <0.2% across frames. The scale bars themselves are the dominant error.

quantities.notes: Sample extents read by eye from gridded frames (+/-20 px), using the px/mm above: M1 gap 420 px = 2.27 mm, perpendicular 560 px = 3.03 mm. M3 gap ~470 px = 2.5-2.65 mm. M4 gap 405 px = 2.51 mm, perpendicular 470 px = 2.92 mm (with the SI bars it would be 1.6 x 1.9 mm, inconsistent with any stated dimension, so the Fig. 3a bar is preferred). M5 gap 700 px = 2.5-2.7 mm, perpendicular 860 px = 3.1-3.3 mm (Methods HP 2.3 x 2.5 does not fit the aspect ratio). M2 gap ~1416 px = 2.9 mm. Recommended: calibrate per movie from the Fig. 3a bar where available, and report the sample-dimension calibration as an independent cross-check (~10-15% disagreement).

quantities.quantity: how movie frames map to experiment time
quantities.notes: Every movie repeats each acquired image for 10 frames (0.4 s). Distinct images: M1 11, M2 14 (first 2.4 s static), M3 51, M4 50, M5 36 (irregular holds in M5). Stated acquisition period is 2-7 s per image, so the playback speed-up is 5x-17.5x. Only Movie 4 has an on-screen clock. There it is 6.9 s/image (median; min 6.4, max 14.1), i.e. ~17.8x.

quantities.quantity: Movie 4 frame -> experiment time and cell voltage, from the on-screen marker

uncertainty.note: 0.74 s per plot pixel; tick-fit residual 0.17 s / 0.006 V

quantities.notes: The on-screen axis matches Supp. Fig. 12's time axis (41.30-41.46 h).

quantities.quantity: voltage events in Movie 4 (consecutive marker samples bracket each event)
quantities.notes: First short occurs 14-28 s after the polarity reversal. Second short occurs 133-146 s after re-plating onset. Expected crossing time from the matched Fig. 3e point (45.3 um/s) with a 2.51 mm gap is ~55 s. Neither event matches cleanly (gap / 14-28 s = 90-180 um/s; gap / 133-146 s = 17-19 um/s). The start-time convention is unknown.
